title: Verified main-sequence M-dwarf rapid rotators of the TESS CPV test are kinematically about 1 Gyr old, so their CPV count excludes a supply decline beyond contraction faster than about 0.15-0.8 Gyr
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period. Stellar contraction, through the corotation-to-stellar radius ratio x, explains the decline of the CPV rate inside 1-750 Myr groups. After blended periods are removed, old main-sequence (MS) M dwarfs at the same x have a rate factor near 0.5 with wide intervals. Whether the age decline is geometric or a decline in the supply of material depends on the age of these MS test stars, which nobody had measured. We first repeated the period attribution with TESS flux-weighted centroids for all 4,595 rapid rotators of the test (6,167 SPOC 2-minute light curves). In agreement with concurrent campaign studies, 48% of MS periods at P < 0.2 d come from another star, and eRASS1 confirms it: 97% of on-target and 14% of off-target MS stars have saturated coronae. With verified rotators the frozen x-only model predicts 4.0-5.3 MS CPVs for 2 observed (BP-RP 2.4-3.8) and 8.4-9.4 for 5 (BP-RP 2.0-4.2); the MS factor is 0.37-0.55 (95% lower bounds 0.06-0.08 and 0.17-0.19). Gaia tangential velocities give a dispersion of 14.2 (13.1-15.2) km/s for the 268 verified MS test stars, against 29.4 km/s for slow-rotating MS M dwarfs and 23.6 km/s for stars with blended periods. With an age-velocity relation calibrated on the slow stars, the mean age is 1.0 Gyr (0.6-1.4 Gyr for slopes 0.3-0.5). A supply factor exp(-t/tau_s) or (t/15 Myr)^-alpha on top of contraction must then have tau_s > 345-375 Myr and alpha < 0.44-0.47 in the colour-wide sample (reference model; 147-792 Myr and 0.36-0.63 over all age models), and tau_s > 42-512 Myr, alpha < 0.57-1.22 in the primary window. A 44-Myr decay (p = 7e-10) and a debris-disk-like t^-1 decay (p = 9e-6) are excluded in the colour-wide sample. Thus contraction is sufficient and a fast-decaying external reservoir is not the cause of the age decline; a factor of about 2 remains allowed. Limitations: 2-5 MS CPVs, an assumed age-velocity relation and age distribution, a frozen rate model, and a 5-arcsec centroid resolution.

display.caption: (a) Tangential velocity dispersion relative to the LSR (Gaia DR3, BP-RP 2.4-3.8, 95% bootstrap intervals): slow-rotating MS M dwarfs, MS stars with off-target (blended) TESS periods, centroid-verified MS rapid rotators by period, the verified MS test stars, and 35-750 Myr members (kinematically selected, for scale). (b, c) MS rate factor predicted by a supply decline exp(-t/tau_s) or (t/15 Myr)^-alpha on top of contraction, averaged over the kinematic age distribution (uniform ages from 0.1 Gyr to the lower 95% value of the fitted upper age) for age-velocity slopes 0.3-0.5; dash-dot lines: 95% lower bounds of the measured factor (centroid + eRASS1 weights).

(a) Frozen x-only CPV model applied to MS rapid rotators (BP-RP 2.4-3.8) with different cleaning: predicted CPVs (95% bootstrap intervals) for all stars in the x range (blue) and neighbour-clean stars (green); crosses: observed. (b) Profile likelihood of the MS rate factor at fixed x; the dashed black curve is the colour-wide sample (BP-RP 2.0-4.2).

(a) Offset of the TESS periodic signal from the Gaia target (flux-weighted centroids) against period for MS rapid rotators, coloured by eRASS1 class; circles: CPVs. (b) eRASS1 saturated fraction (95% profile intervals) by centroid class and group.
